title: 10 of 15 suburban wards but 2 of 9 island-city wards are in the two highest incident classes - and ward population alone ranks wards with Spearman rho = 0.83
method: Ordinal incident class per ward digitised from BMC FPG 2026 p.18 (colour-matched to legend, 3 sample points per ward, 24/24 unanimous); population from Census 2011 aggregated to wards.
caveats: Counts are complaint/incident records (source: 'CCS'), so they reflect reporting as well as flooding.
Only the class bin is known, not the exact count.

title: Three official lists name 251 distinct places, but only 16 (6%) appear on more than one list
method: Same-ward matching: fuzzy name tokens (Jaccard >= 0.5, >= 2 shared tokens) or geocodes within 250 m plus partial name match; never merging two records of one source. Edition similarity = word-level SequenceMatcher ratio of BEST Annex IX text.
period: BMC FPG 2026 (incl. Mumbai Traffic Police table); BEST booklets 2023-24, 2024-25, 2026
sample: 97 BMC rows (24 wards), 84 BEST rows (9 island-city wards), 90 traffic-police rows (19 ward headings)
caveats: The lists serve different purposes (BMC: dewatering pumps; BEST: switching off electricity; traffic police: diversions), so they need not match - but none can be treated as complete.
Name matching can miss the same place written very differently, so overlap may be understated.

title: Monsoon rain is extremely concentrated, and global-model rainfall misses Mumbai's extremes
method: IMD monthly grid 19.00N 72.75E (1901-2021); ERA5 daily via Open-Meteo (1991-2025); Theil-Sen slope + Kendall tau for trends; heavy day = IMD category >= 64.5 mm/24 h.
caveats: ERA5 is a ~25 km model estimate; both Mumbai reference points fall in one cell, so it cannot show rainfall differences between neighbourhoods.
The 944 mm figure is a station record quoted by BMC; ERA5 is an area average, so some gap is expected - the size of the gap is the point.

title: Terrain (90 m DEM) does not clearly separate listed spots from the rest of their ward
method: Copernicus GLO-90 DEM via Open-Meteo; TPI = elevation minus median of 500 m grid cells within 1 km; each location's percentile among its own ward's grid cells; Wilcoxon signed-rank vs 0.5.
caveats: GLO-90 is a 90 m surface model including buildings; vertical error is metres.
Geocoding error (tens to hundreds of metres) blurs the comparison.
Listed spots are not a random sample of flooded places.

title: 43 of 97 BMC-listed spots have no dewatering pump recorded against them
method: Direct counts from the transcribed BMC FPG 2026 ward directory.
caveats: A blank pump cell may mean no pump, a pump recorded elsewhere, or a mitigated spot - the source does not say.
Capacity figures are incomplete for several multi-pump spots.
